subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu support automatic group-sender agent provisioning, and what identity, authorization, quota/lifecycle, and shared/private memory boundaries should become the public contract?
rationale: The request changes durable agent creation, workspace/config mutation, memory isolation, routing authority, and cost/security boundaries rather than only fixing a Feishu session-key bug.

options.title: Design the generic contract first
options.body: Approve a channel-agnostic identity-to-agent lifecycle, authorization, quota, and shared/private memory contract before implementing Feishu support.

options.title: Keep explicit routing only
options.body: Retain group session scoping plus explicit thread-bound subagents and document external fleet patterns instead of automatic provisioning.

options.title: Decline automatic provisioning
options.body: Close this direction if group chat sender identities should not automatically create durable OpenClaw agents.

recommendation.title: Design the generic contract first
recommendation.body: Approve a channel-agnostic identity-to-agent lifecycle, authorization, quota, and shared/private memory contract before implementing Feishu support.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans Feishu routing, plugin API boundaries, subagent semantics, memory/security policy, and core-lean product direction.
